name: BBQ Chicken and Rice Casserole
description: Comforting casserole with shredded chicken, broccoli rice, and BBQ sauce topped with crispy bacon
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F
Melt butter in a large sauté pan over medium heat, add broccoli rice and season with salt
Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened, then remove from heat
Add cooked white rice, garlic powder, pepper, and remaining salt to the pan with broccoli
Transfer to an 8-inch square casserole dish
Toss shredded chicken with BBQ sauce and spread on top of the rice mixture
Top with bacon and bake for 30 minutes until top is starting to brown
Garnish with green onions and serve

name: White Chicken Chili
description: Creamy and flavorful chicken chili with white beans, green chilis, and lime
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
Add onion and garlic, sauté for 3-4 minutes until translucent
Add green chilis and cook for 1 minute until fragrant
Add shredded chicken and seasonings, stir to combine
Pour in broth, increase heat, stir in beans and corn
Cover and simmer for 10 minutes
Turn off heat and stir in sour cream, lime juice, and bacon
Garnish with avocado, cilantro, and lime wedges

name: Chicken and Broccoli Fried Rice
description: Quick Asian-inspired fried rice with tender chicken, broccoli, and scrambled eggs
instructions: Heat 2 tsp oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat
Add whisked eggs and scramble until cooked, set aside
Add 1 tbsp oil to pan, then ginger and garlic, cook 30 seconds
Add broccoli and carrots, cook 3-4 minutes until slightly browned
Add chicken and green onions, sauté 1-2 minutes
Add remaining oil, rice, coconut aminos, sesame oil, salt, and pepper flakes
Cook undisturbed 2-3 minutes, stir, then cook another 2-3 minutes
Add scrambled eggs back, garnish with green onions and cilantro

name: Spinach Artichoke Meatza
description: Pizza with a ground beef crust topped with creamy spinach and artichoke mixture
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F
Soften cream cheese in microwave, stir in garlic powder and salt
Heat oil in a skillet, add garlic and sauté 30 seconds
Add spinach and sauté 1 minute until wilted
Drain artichokes and add to skillet with mushrooms and Italian seasoning
Spread cream cheese mixture over par-baked meatza crust
Top with spinach-artichoke mixture
Bake until warmed through and edges are crispy

name: Enchilada-Stuffed Zucchini Boats
description: Hollowed zucchini filled with seasoned ground beef in enchilada sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F
Stir ground beef into enchilada sauce
Place zucchini halves in casserole dish
Brush boats with oil and season with salt and pepper
Fill each zucchini half with meat sauce
Top with cheese
Bake for 25 minutes until cheese is browned and zucchini is cooked
Serve with cilantro-lime cauliflower rice

name: Ground Beef Stroganoff
description: Classic stroganoff with mushrooms served over zucchini noodles
instructions: Heat butter in a large skillet over medium heat
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened
Add cooked ground beef and mushrooms
Stir in broth, coconut aminos, and Dijon mustard
Simmer for 5-10 minutes until sauce thickens
Remove from heat and stir in sour cream
Season with salt and pepper
Serve over zucchini noodles, garnish with parsley

name: Cottage Pie
description: Hearty ground beef filling topped with creamy mashed potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F
Heat oil in a large skillet, cook onion and garlic until softened
Add ground beef and cook until browned
Stir in tomato paste, broth, and seasonings
Simmer until sauce thickens
Transfer to a baking dish
Top with mashed potatoes, spreading evenly
Bake 25-30 minutes until potatoes are golden

name: Green Chili Chicken Casserole
description: Creamy chicken casserole with green chilis and Mexican flavors
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F
Mix cream cheese, sour cream, and green chilis
Layer chicken in a baking dish
Spread cream cheese mixture over chicken
Top with cheese
Bake 25-30 minutes until bubbly
Let rest 5 minutes before serving
Garnish with cilantro

name: Chicken Parmesan Bake
description: Easy baked chicken parmesan without the breading
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F
Place chicken breasts in a baking dish
Season with Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper
Top each breast with marinara sauce
Sprinkle with mozzarella and parmesan
Bake 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through
Broil 2-3 minutes to brown cheese
Garnish with fresh basil

name: Balsamic Chicken Sheet Pan Dinner
description: One-pan roasted chicken with vegetables and balsamic glaze
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F
Arrange chicken thighs and vegetables on a sheet pan
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar
Season with Italian herbs, salt, and pepper
Roast for 35-40 minutes until chicken is cooked through
Vegetables should be tender and caramelized
Drizzle with additional balsamic before serving

name: Picadillo Tacos
description: Cuban-style ground beef with olives and raisins in lettuce wraps
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat
Add onion and cook until softened
Add ground beef and cook until browned
Stir in tomato sauce, olives, and raisins
Season with cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper
Simmer for 10 minutes
Serve in lettuce cups with fresh toppings

name: Turkey Taco Skillet
description: Quick one-pan turkey taco meat with peppers and tomatoes
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
Add ground turkey and cook until browned
Add bell peppers and onion, cook until softened
Stir in diced tomatoes and taco seasoning
Simmer for 5-10 minutes
Serve with your choice of toppings

name: Brisket and Potato Hash
description: Hearty hash with tender brisket, potatoes, and peppers
instructions: Heat oil in a large cast-iron skillet
Add diced potatoes and cook until crispy
Add bell peppers and onion, cook until softened
Add shredded brisket and seasonings
Create wells and crack eggs into them
Cover and cook until eggs are set
Serve immediately

name: Roasted Chicken with Green Beans
description: Simple roasted chicken with garlicky green beans and potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F
Place chicken on a sheet pan with potatoes
Season with herbs and drizzle with oil
Roast for 30 minutes
Add green beans to the pan
Continue roasting 15 minutes until chicken is cooked
Let rest before serving

name: Shredded Beef Tacos
description: Slow-cooked shredded beef with smoky chipotle flavors
instructions: Season beef roast with salt and pepper
Place in slow cooker with onion, garlic, and chipotles
Add broth and cook on low for 8 hours
Shred beef with two forks
Serve in tortillas or lettuce wraps
Top with fresh salsa, avocado, and cilantro

name: Pork Carnitas Bowl
description: Crispy slow-cooked pork with rice, beans, and fresh toppings
instructions: Season pork shoulder with cumin, oregano, and salt
Place in slow cooker with orange juice and garlic
Cook on low for 8 hours until very tender
Shred pork and broil to crisp
Serve over rice with black beans
Top with fresh salsa, cheese, and lime

name: Chicken Sausage and Vegetable Bake
description: Easy sheet pan dinner with chicken sausage and roasted vegetables
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F
Cut sausages and vegetables into chunks
Toss everything with olive oil and seasonings
Spread on a sheet pan in a single layer
Roast for 25-30 minutes until vegetables are tender
Stir halfway through cooking

name: Asian Beef Lettuce Wraps
description: Savory ground beef with Asian flavors in crispy lettuce cups
instructions: Heat oil in a large skillet over high heat
Add ground beef and cook until browned
Add garlic, ginger, and water chestnuts
Stir in coconut aminos and sesame oil
Cook until sauce thickens
Serve in butter lettuce cups
Top with green onions and sesame seeds

name: Lemon Herb Salmon
description: Baked salmon with fresh herbs and lemon
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F
Place salmon fillets on a baking sheet
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice
Season with herbs, salt, and pepper
Bake for 12-15 minutes until flaky
Garnish with fresh dill and lemon slices

name: Tuscan Chicken Skillet
description: Creamy sun-dried tomato chicken with spinach
instructions: Season chicken with Italian herbs
Sear chicken in a hot skillet, set aside
Sauté garlic and sun-dried tomatoes
Add broth and cream, simmer
Add spinach and return chicken to pan
Cook until chicken is done and spinach wilted
Garnish with parmesan

name: Bacon Burgers with Broccoli and Twice-Baked Fries
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: slices white cheddar cheese or other cheese of choice

instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread out the fries on one half of the lined baking sheet and toss with the olive oil.
On the other half of the baking sheet, spread out the broccoli.
Bake for 15 minutes, until both the fries and the broccoli are warmed through and slightly crisp.
For the burgers:
While the fries and broccoli are baking, preheat a grill to high heat.

Once the grill is at temperature, sear the burger patties for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, until they develop char marks and are medium to medium-well done. (Alternatively, you can cook the burgers in a skillet over medium-high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side.) After ͆ipping, top the burgers with cheese and bacon.
Once cooked, transfer to a plate to rest.
While the burgers are resting, slice the tomato(es) and avocado, if using.
Plate the burgers, top with the tomato and avocado slices, and serve alongside the fries and broccoli!
If desired, use butter lettuce leaves as “buns.”

name: Cajun Chicken and Rice Skillet
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings

ingredients.name: fresh lemon juice (about ½ small lemon)

instructions: To make the Cajun chicken, melt the butter in a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Once melted, add the peppers, onion, and garlic and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until browned, then transfer the vegetables to a large bowl and set aside.
Cut the lemon in half and place the halves cut side down in the pan for 1 to 2 minutes, until browned, then set aside.
Add the sausage and chicken to the pan and cook until slightly browned, 3 to 5 minutes, then transfer to the bowl with the vegetables.
To make the rice, melt the butter in the same pan.
Once melted, add the rest of the ingredients for the rice and stir to combine.
Cook until warmed through, scraping the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon to release the charred bits.
Top the rice with the veggies, sausage, and chicken and garnish with the parsley and charred lemon halves, then serve.
I know that at ͅrst glance, ground chicken, bell peppers, and rice don’t sound like the most inspiring ingredients, but hang in there.

name: Curried Chicken Lettuce Cups
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: To make the chicken ͅlling, heat the ghee in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the bell peppers and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly browned.
Meanwhile, juice the lime and set aside.
Add the garlic to the pan with the bell peppers and cook for 30 seconds, or until fragrant.
Add the chicken, green onions, curry powder, ginger powder, and salt to the pan and stir to combine.
Add the broth, coconut aminos, and lime juice and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the chicken is warmed through and the broth has evaporated.
Meanwhile, cut ½ lime into wedges for serving.
Stir the cilantro into the chicken mixture, then remove from the heat.
Spoon the chicken into the lettuce leaves and serve with lime wedges!
Firecracker Meatballs Precooked meatballs Sriracha-lime sauce
Place the meatballs and sauce in a large saucepan over medium heat and toss to coat.
Cover and cook for 5 minutes, or until the meatballs are warmed through.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium-sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving it for about 2 minutes, until hot.
Serve the meatballs alongside the rice and garnish with the sliced green onions.

name: Chicken Burrito Bowls
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: To make the pepper and onion topping, heat the oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Once hot, add the peppers and onion and season with ½ teaspoon of the salt.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 7 to 8 minutes, until the peppers and onion are limp and slightly browned.
Meanwhile, prepare the ingredients for serving: Slice the avocado, dice the red onion, and cut the lime into ͅve wedges.
When the peppers and onion are done, remove them from the pan and set aside.
To make the chicken topping, add the chicken to the sauté pan along with the broth, lime juice, spices, and remaining ½ teaspoon of salt.
Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the broth has evaporated, then remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium-sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving it for about 2 minutes, until hot.
Stir the salt, lime juice, and cilantro into the rice.
To assemble the burrito bowls, divide the rice among ͅve bowls, then add the pepper/onion and chicken toppings.
Garnish with the avocado slices and diced red onion and serve with lime wedges!

name: Roasted Tomato Soup and Grilled Turkey and Cheese Sandwiches
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: slices white cheddar cheese or other cheese of choice

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a medium-sized saucepan over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the onion and garlic.
Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion starts to brown and the garlic is fragrant.
Measure out ¼ cup of the basil leaves and tear each leaf in half, setting the rest aside for garnish.
Add the torn basil leaves to the pan along with the remaining soup ingredients and stir to combine.
Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, then either blend in the pan with an immersion blender or transfer the soup to a blender and carefully blend until smooth.
Return the soup to the pan, then taste for seasoning and add more salt, if needed.
Reduce the heat to low to keep the soup warm while you make the sandwiches.
To make the grilled cheese sandwiches:
Place a skillet large enough to ͅt at least two sandwiches over medium-low heat.
For each sandwich, layer a slice of cheese, one-quarter of the turkey, and another slice of cheese between two slices of bread.
Spread 1 tablespoon of butter on the outside of each slice of bread.
Place two sandwiches in the skillet and cook for about 2 minutes, until the cheese is starting to melt and the bread is golden brown.
Carefully ͆ip the sandwiches and cook for an additional 2 minutes, until the cheese is fully melted and the bread is golden brown.
Repeat with the remaining bread, butter, cheese, and turkey to make two more sandwiches.
While the second set of sandwiches is toasting, cut the remaining basil into ribbons: Stack the leaves, then roll them up and thinly slice them.
Cut the sandwiches in half and serve alongside the hot tomato soup garnished with the sliced basil.
Enjoy!

name: Turkey Casserole
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: bacon, cooked and chopped or crumbled

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Spread the potatoes in a 3-quart casserole dish or 2½-quart Dutch oven.
In a large bowl, whisk together the hot sauce and melted butter.
Add the turkey and toss to coat.
Layer the turkey and sauce on top of the potatoes in the casserole dish, then top with the bacon.
Bake the casserole for 30 minutes, until completely warmed through.
While the casserole is in the oven, thinly slice the green onions and chop the parsley.
Remove the casserole from the oven and allow to cool slightly.
Drizzle with the ranch dressing, then garnish with the sliced green onions and chopped parsley and serve!

name: Turkey Pizza Sheet Pan Dinner
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Toss the turkey with the ranch dressing, then spread the turkey on the lined baking sheet.
Cut the tomatoes in half and sprinkle them on top of the turkey.
Follow with the potatoes and then the cheese.
Layer the pepperoni, mushrooms, black olives, and bell pepper on top of the cheese.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the toppings are browned and the cheese is bubbly.
Garnish with the red pepper ͆akes and serve!

name: Taco Casserole
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: can mild diced tomatoes and green chilis

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Put all of the ingredients for the rice layer in a large bowl and mix to combine, then spread the mixture in an 8 by 11-inch or similar-sized baking dish.
Mix together the ingredients for the beef layer, then layer the beef mixture on top of the rice.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the casserole is hot and the beef is browned on top.
While the casserole is baking, dice the avocado.
Remove the casserole from the oven, top it with the lettuce, avocado, tomato, jalapeño, and red onion, and serve!

name: Korean Beef Bowls
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of the ghee in a large skillet over medium heat.
Once hot, add the ground beef and green onions.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onions have wilted, then pour the Korean sauce over the beef mixture.
Cook for an additional 4 to 5 minutes, until warmed through.
Meanwhile, fry the eggs: Heat the remaining ½ tablespoon of ghee in a large skillet over medium heat.
Crack the eggs into the skillet and fry for about 4 minutes, or until done to your liking.
Reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium-sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving it for about 2 minutes, until hot.
To serve, divide the warmed rice, beef mixture, and pickled carrots evenly among ͅve bowls.
Top each bowl with a fried egg, some green onions, Sriracha mayo, sesame seeds, and a sprinkle of red pepper ͆akes, if using, and serve!

name: Confetti Chicken Casserole
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: bacon, cooked and sliced or crumbled

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
In a large bowl, stir together the onion and bell pepper mixture, corn, kale, chicken, mayonnaise, salt, and pepper until combined.
Transfer the chicken mixture to a 3-quart rectangular casserole dish, then top with the cheese and bacon.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the cheese is browned and bubbling.
Meanwhile, slice the green onion and set aside.
Let the casserole cool slightly, then garnish with green onion and serve!

name: Mexican Chicken and Corn Street Tacos
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: miniature corn tortillas, or 8 regular-size corn tortillas

instructions: Make the slaw: In a small bowl, toss the kale with the chipotle-lime dressing until it is fully coated.
Set aside.
Make the chicken ͅlling: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once melted, add the chicken and corn and cook for 2 minutes to warm through.
Add the lime juice, salt, chili powder, garlic powder, and paprika and toss to coat the chicken and corn.
Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes, until the chicken is slightly browned.
Place a small skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, put one tortilla in the pan at a time and warm for about 30 seconds per side, until the tortilla is pliable and begins to brown slightly.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
To keep the tortillas warm while you are heating the remaining ones, you can wrap them in a kitchen towel.
To assemble the tacos, top the warmed tortillas with the kale slaw and chicken ͅlling and garnish with the Cotija cheese.
Serve with lime wedges.
Green Goddess Salad Green goddess dressing, divided or frozen corn kernels, thawed
Toss the kale with 1/3 cup of the dressing until well coated.
Cube the avocado.
Divide the dressed kale among four plates.
Top each serving evenly with the corn, chicken, avocado, and bacon.
Serve with the remaining dressing on the side.

name: Philly Cheesesteak Loaded Fries
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Place the potato wedges and 1½ teaspoons of the olive oil in a medium-sized bowl and toss to coat.
Spread the potato wedges on a rimmed baking sheet.
In another medium-sized bowl, toss the brisket with the remaining oil, salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Arrange the seasoned beef on top of the fries.
Spread the peppers and onions on top of the beef, then top with the cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the cheese is browned and bubbling.
Sprinkle with the dried parsley and serve!

name: Gyro Salad with Garlic Potato Wedges
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt or dairy-free Greek-style yogurt

instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Toss the potato wedges with the olive oil and garlic powder and lay on one-half of a rimmed baking sheet.
Toss the brisket with one-third of the Greek dressing, then lay the beef on the other half of the baking sheet.
Bake the potatoes and brisket for 10 minutes, until warmed through and slightly browned.
While the potatoes and beef are baking, make the salad: Put the lettuce, diced cucumbers, olives, red onion, and feta in a large serving bowl.
If using grape tomatoes, slice them in half and add them to the bowl.
Toss the salad and set aside.
To make the tzatziki, peel and shred the cucumber, then roll it up in a dish towel or cheesecloth and squeeze until all of the moisture is released.
Place the drained cucumber in a small bowl along with the yogurt, garlic, and salt.
Stir to combine and set aside.
When the potatoes and beef are ͅnished baking, place them on top of the salad, then drizzle with the remaining dressing.
Serve with the tzatziki for dipping!

name: Lemon Ginger Chicken Stir-Fry
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Heat the oil in a large sauté pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the green beans and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender.
Remove the beans from the pan and set aside.
Add the chicken to the pan and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 to 5 minutes, until warmed through and slightly browned.
Return the green beans to the pan with the chicken, then pour the sauce over the beans and chicken and stir to combine.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce is warmed, then remove from the heat.
Garnish with the sesame seeds and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Chicken Vesuvio
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a medium-sized saucepan over medium heat.
Once hot, add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute, until browned.
Add the white wine and broth and bring to a simmer.
Continue to simmer for 5 minutes, until reduced slightly, then remove the pan from the heat.
Meanwhile, recrisp the chicken and cook/reheat the vegetables.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons of oil in a large cast-iron skillet or heavy sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Sear the chicken pieces, skin side down, for 5 to 7 minutes, or until crisp.
If the chicken skin sticks to the pan, add more oil as needed to prevent sticking.
Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add the onion to the cast-iron skillet and cook for 3 minutes, or until translucent.
Then add the green beans, potatoes, peas, salt, and pepper and toss to combine.
Whisk the butter and lemon juice into the thickened wine and garlic sauce, then pour it over the green bean and potato mixture.
Nestle the chicken into the pan, skin side up, and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook for 5 minutes, until everything is fully reheated and the sauce is bubbling.
Garnish with the lemon slices and parsley, then serve!

name: Italian Beef Rolls with Vodka Sauce
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Put the beef in a bowl and toss with the Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Place about ¼ cup of the seasoned beef on the bottom third of a collard leaf, then fold the sides of the leaf over the beef ͅlling and roll.
Place the collard roll, folded side down, in a 3-quart rectangular casserole dish.
Repeat with the remaining collard leaves and beef.
Pour the vodka sauce over the collard rolls, then bake for 20 minutes, until the sauce has browned slightly on top.
Garnish with the chopped basil and serve!

name: Red Curry Acorn Squash Soup with Crispy Beef
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: ghee, avocado oil, or other fat of choice

instructions: Put all of the soup ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth, then pour the soup into a large pot.
Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes or until fully warmed through.
While the soup is heating, prepare the beef: Place the ghee in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Put the beef, spices, salt, and coconut aminos in a medium- sized bowl and toss to combine.
Once the ghee is hot, add the seasoned beef to the pan, spreading it across the surface of the pan.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp, then ͆ip and cook for an additional 3 to 4 minutes, until browned and crisp on the other side.
Serve the soup in bowls topped with the shredded beef and garnished with the cilantro.

name: Sweet-and-Sour Chicken Chow Mein
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Put the ghee in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the bell peppers and onion.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the onion is translucent and the peppers are slightly browned and wilted.
Add the chicken and pineapple, then pour in the sauce and cook for an additional chow mein.
For the chow mein:
Place the ghee in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the cabbage and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until wilted, then add the squash and teriyaki sauce and toss to coat.
Cook for an additional 2 to 3 minutes, until warmed through.
Add the green onions and stir to combine, then garnish with the sesame seeds.
Serve the sweet-and-sour chicken alongside the chow mein.

name: Chicken Souvlaki Bowls
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings

ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt or dairy-free Greek-style yogurt

instructions: To make the tzatziki, peel and shred the cucumber, or until you have about 3 tablespoons, then roll it up in a dish towel or cheesecloth and squeeze until all of the excess moisture is released from the cucumber.
Place the drained cucumber in a small bowl along with the yogurt, garlic, and salt.
Stir to combine, then store in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
Put the chicken in a large skillet over medium heat, then pour in half of the dressing; reserve the other half for serving.
Toss to coat the chicken with the dressing.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then ͆ip the chicken.
Add the roasted peppers to the skillet and cook for an additional 2 to 3 minutes, until the peppers are warmed and the chicken is browned, then remove from the heat.
While the peppers are warming, reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium- sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving it for about 2 minutes, until hot.
Meanwhile, chop the parsley leaves and cut the tomato into four wedges.
When the rice is warmed, stir in the chopped parsley.
To assemble the bowls, divide the lettuce evenly among ͅve bowls, then top the lettuce evenly with the rice, chicken and peppers, cucumber slices, tomato wedges, and olives.
Serve with the tzatziki and the remaining Greek dressing on the side.

name: Chicken Tetrazzini
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: gluten-free ͆our blend, or 1 tablespoon arrowroot powder
heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Place the butter in a medium-sized saucepan over medium heat.
Once melted, add the ͆our and whisk until smooth.
Slowly pour in the broth, whisking constantly to smooth out any lumps, then whisk in the heavy cream, salt, and pepper.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then stir in the chicken, peas, and cooked mushroom mixture.
Simmer for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Layer the squash strands in a 9 by 13-inch baking dish, then spoon the chicken mixture over the squash.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the top is slightly bubbly, then remove from the oven.
Let cool slightly, then garnish with the parsley and serve! note: If using arrowroot powder, omit the butter and skip Steps 2 and 3.
Instead, combine the broth, cream, salt, and pepper in a medium-sized saucepan and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
In a small bowl, mix together 1 tablespoon arrowroot powder and 2 tablespoons water.
Once the broth mixture is boiling, pour in the arrowroot slurry and bring back up to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer until thickened, 1 to 2 minutes, then proceed with Step 4.
I know I’m not supposed to play favorites, but if I had to choose just one week’s worth of meals to make over and over again, it would undoubtedly be this one.

name: Beef Ragu
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Make the ragu: Bring the tomato sauce to a simmer in a large pot over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the shredded beef to the sauce and stir to combine, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the meat is warmed through.
Taste the sauce and season with salt, if needed.
While the ragu is cooking, make the noodles: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Once hot, add the zucchini noodles and sauté for 4 to 5 minutes, until the zucchini is reduced in volume and cooked through.
Drain oﬀ any excess water.
Stir the sliced kale into the ragu and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the kale is wilted and turns bright green.
Serve the ragu with the zucchini noodles, garnished with the shaved Parmesan and some freshly ground pepper.
This is one of those weeks that just makes a lot of sense!
These recipes transform ground beef, spinach, and spaghetti squash into classic comfort foods, but with a twist.

name: Bolognese Casserole
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Toss the squash strands with the olive oil, parsley, garlic powder, and salt, then place in a 3-quart baking dish.
Top the squash mixture with the Bolognese sauce, then bake for 20 minutes, until the top is slightly browned and bubbling.
Meanwhile, chop the parsley and set aside.
Garnish the casserole with the parsley and Parmesan cheese and serve!

name: Mediterranean Skillet
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large cast-iron skillet or sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
Add the artichoke hearts and tomatoes and cook, stirring occasionally, for an additional 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly browned.
Meanwhile, juice the lemons until you have about ¼ cup of juice.
Set aside.
Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the pan with the tomatoes and artichokes, then stir in the spinach and cook for about 1 minute, until the spinach is wilted.
Mix in the beef.
Add the lemon juice, salt, and seasonings and toss to combine.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes to let the ͆avors combine.
Meanwhile, chop the parsley.
Garnish the mixture in the skillet with the olives, feta, and chopped parsley and serve!

name: Spinach Pesto Spaghetti Squash Boats
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Use a fork to scrape the squash strands from the shells, reserving the shells.
In a large bowl, toss the squash strands with the spinach pesto and salt.
Stuﬀ the mixture back into the shells and top with the meatballs.
Bake for 15 minutes or until fully warmed through, then garnish with the Parmesan cheese and serve!

name: Al Pastor Pizzas
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Place an oven rack in the lower position.
Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Spread the shredded pork and pineapple over the pizza crusts, then top with the adobo sauce.
Place the pizzas directly on the lower oven rack and bake for 15 minutes, until the pork is browned and the sauce is bubbling.
Garnish with the cilantro and red onion, then slice and serve!

name: Green Pork Chili
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings

ingredients.name: sour cream or cream scooped from the top of 1 (13½-ounce) can chilled full-fat coconut milk
bunch Lacinato (aka dinosaur) kale, destemmed and chopped

instructions: In a large pot over medium heat, whisk together the chicken broth, salsa, sour cream, lime juice, and seasonings, then stir in the shredded pork and kale.
Let the chili come to a slight simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 15 minutes.
Serve in bowls and garnish with the fresh cilantro and sour cream.
Caribbean Plantain Bowls Pan-fried plantains Wilted kale Garlic sauce
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the plantains and cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until warmed through.
Remove from the pan and set aside.
Add the wilted kale to the skillet and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until warmed through.
Remove from the pan and set aside.
Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the skillet and evenly spread the shredded pork over the pan.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp on the bottom, then ͆ip and cook for an additional 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp on the other side.
Assemble the bowls with the crispy pork, plantains, and kale.
Drizzle with the garlic sauce and serve!

name: Crusted Chicken Pot Pie
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: salted butter, ghee, or oil of choice

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Melt the butter in a Dutch oven or other heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat, then add the onion and garlic.
Sauté for 4 to 5 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
Sprinkle the ͆our over the onion mixture and whisk to combine.
Pour in the broth 1 cup at a time, whisking constantly, then add the cream, sage, thyme, salt, and pepper, continuing to whisk until the mixture is smooth.
Stir in the chicken and the peas and carrots.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
While the chicken mixture is simmering, rewarm the potato-parsnip mash in the microwave for 3 minutes or in a covered saucepan on the stovetop over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes.
It should have a spreadable consistency.
Transfer the chicken mixture to a 4-quart casserole dish or deep-sided ovenproof sauté pan, then top with the potato-parsnip mash.
Bake for 30 minutes, until browned and bubbly on top.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly, then garnish with the parsley and serve! note: If using arrowroot powder instead of the gluten-free ͆our blend, skip Step 3 and pick up with Step 4.

When the broth begins to bubble in Step 5, whisk 2 teaspoons arrowroot powder with 2 tablespoons water to make a slurry, then pour the slurry into the chicken mixture, whisking constantly, and return it to a simmer.
Continue to cook for 1 minute, until thickened.
Buﬀalo

name: Cashew Chicken
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add 1 tablespoon of the avocado oil and swirl it around the pan.
Add the bell pepper strips and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly browned.
Add the broccoli ͆orets and snow peas to the pan.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables begin to soften.
Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the pan, then add the chicken, green onions, and toasted cashews.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the chicken is warmed through, then pour the stir-fry sauce over the chicken mixture and toss to coat.
To reheat the rice, place it in a medium-sized saucepan over low heat, covered, for 5 minutes or microwave for 2 minutes, or until hot.
Garnish with the sesame seeds and serve with the rice.

name: Twice-Baked Loaded Butternut Squash
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: plain full-fat Greek yogurt or dairy-free Greek-style yogurt
bacon, cooked and sliced or crumbled

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Place the squash halves on a rimmed baking sheet, then scoop the pulp out of the shells into a medium-sized bowl, leaving a ½-inch-thick wall of squash in the shells.
To the squash pulp, add the yogurt, salt, garlic powder, thyme, and rosemary.
Mash with a potato masher or blend with an immersion blender until fully incorporated, then stir in the bacon.
Taste for seasoning and add more salt, if needed.
Spoon the squash mixture back into the shells and top with the cubed turkey.
Bake for 25 minutes, until warmed through and slightly browned on top.
To serve, cut the squash halves in half to create four portions.
Divide among four plates and snip the chives over the top, if using.

name: Tuscan Turkey Kale Soup
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: carrots, peeled and sliced into ¼-inch-thick coins
bunch Lacinato (aka dinosaur) kale, destemmed and chopped

instructions: Place the shredded turkey, carrots, tomatoes, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, ½ teaspoon of salt, and pepper in a large soup pot with a lid.
Pour in the broth and stir to combine.
Bring to a low boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cover.
Simmer for 15 minutes, until the carrots are soft.
Stir the kale into the soup, then cover and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until the kale is bright green and wilted.
Remove from the heat and stir in the lemon juice.
Taste for seasoning, add up to

name: Harvest Casserole
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings

ingredients.name: chopped fresh sage, or 1 teaspoon dried rubbed sage

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Place the butternut squash pulp, butter, sage, ½ teaspoon of salt, and pepper in a large bowl and mash with a potato masher or blend with an immersion blender.
Taste for seasoning and add up to ½ teaspoon more salt, if needed.
Spread the squash mixture in an 8-inch baking dish or similar-sized enameled cast-iron pan, then top with the wilted kale.
Next, layer on the cubed turkey.
To make the topping, whisk together the butter, honey, cinnamon, and salt in a small bowl, then add the pecans and toss to coat.
Sprinkle the pecans on top of the casserole.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the casserole is warmed through and the pecans are toasted.
Top with the pomegranate seeds and serve!

name: Smashed Sweet Potato and Pork Bowls
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings

ingredients.name: salted butter, ghee, or other fat of choice

instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut the sweet potatoes crosswise into 1-inch-thick rounds and place on the lined baking sheet, then smash the potatoes with a metal spatula to a ¼-inch thickness.
Brush the sweet potatoes with the melted butter and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon of the salt.
Bake for 15 minutes, until slightly browned and crisp on top.
While the potatoes are cooking, place the oil in a large sauté pan over medium- high heat.
Once hot, add the shredded pork, oregano, pepper, and remaining teaspoon of salt to the pan.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the pork is crisp, then ͆ip and cook for an additional 2 to 3 minutes, until it is browned and crisp on the other side.
Remove the pork from the pan and set aside.
Add the Brussels sprouts and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 to 5 minutes, until heated through, then remove the pan from the heat.
Assemble the bowls: Place two or three sweet potato rounds in each bowl and divide the pork and Brussels sprouts evenly among the bowls.
Drizzle with the aioli before serving.

name: Harvest Sheet Pan Dinner
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Cut the apple into ½-inch wedges, discarding the core.
In a medium-sized bowl, toss the apple and onion wedges in 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and the thyme, then spread out on the lined baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes, until softened.
While the apple and onion are cooking, cut the pork shoulder into 1-inch slices.
Then whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil, the balsamic vinegar, and garlic powder in a large bowl and toss the pork and Brussels sprouts in this mixture.

Lay the pork and Brussels sprouts on the baking sheet with the apple and onion, sprinkle the remaining 2 tablespoons of salt over the pork, lay the thyme sprigs on top, and bake for an additional 15 minutes, until the pork is browned.
Let cool slightly, then serve!
Southwestern Stuﬀed

name: Chipotle Chicken Casserole
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Place the paprika, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and mayonnaise in a medium-sized bowl and whisk until smooth.
Add the chicken and toss to coat.
Place the cubed sweet potatoes in a deep 8-inch square casserole dish, then layer the collard greens on top and cover with the chicken mixture.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the top is slightly browned and the casserole is warmed through.

Remove from the oven, drizzle with the cilantro-lime sauce, garnish with the chopped cilantro, if using, and serve! note: To make this dish egg-free, omit the mayo and whisk together the paprika, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, and salt with 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice.
Buﬀalo Chicken–Stuﬀed

name: Chicken Florentine Lasagna
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk
fresh lemon juice (about ½ small lemon)

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Heat the olive oil in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the onion, garlic, and mushrooms.
Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until the onion and mushrooms are beginning to brown and the garlic is fragrant.
Add the collard greens and sun-dried tomatoes, then pour in the wine, broth, heavy cream, and lemon juice.
Season with the salt.
Stir to combine, then simmer for 3 to 5 minutes, until the liquid has reduced slightly.
Place ½ cup of the collard green mixture in a 2-quart rectangular casserole dish, then layer half of the lasagna noodles on top.
Layer half of the remaining collard green mixture on top of the noodles, followed by half of the chicken, then repeat the layers.
Bake for 15 minutes, then top with the Parmesan cheese and return the casserole to the oven to bake for another 15 minutes, until the sauce is bubbly around the edges and the cheese is browned.
Remove from the oven and let cool slightly, then cut and serve!
What a fun week this is!
You are going to transform the wonderfully aﬀordable ground beef, cabbage, and carrots into three fantastic dinners that your family will love.

name: Italian Wedding Soup
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a soup pot that has a lid over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the onion, garlic, and carrots.
Sauté for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is translucent and the carrots are slightly browned.
Add the broth, meatballs, salt, pepper, escarole, cabbage, and parsley to the pot.
Cover with the lid and cook for 5 minutes, until the escarole and cabbage are tender.
Place the eggs and Parmesan cheese in a small bowl and whisk together.
While stirring the simmering soup, slowly pour in the egg mixture until thin strands of eggs form, about 1 minute.
Stir in the lemon juice, then taste for seasoning and add more salt, if needed.
Remove from the heat and serve!

name: Texas Beef Chili
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: salted butter, ghee, or oil of choice
plus 2 tablespoons Texas Chili Spice Blend

instructions: Melt the butter in a soup pot over medium-high heat.
Once melted, add the onion and sauté for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
Then add the garlic and continue cooking for 2 to 3 minutes, until the onion starts to develop a light brown color and the garlic is fragrant.
Add the ground beef and stir to combine.
Then add the spice blend and cook for an additional 2 minutes, or until the spices become fragrant.
Add the strained tomatoes and broth, stir to combine, and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes, or until some of the liquid has evaporated.
While the chili is simmering, reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium- sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving it for about 2 minutes, until hot.
Serve the chili over the warmed rice and garnish with the sour cream and jalapeño slices.

name: Asian Beef Lettuce Cups
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Melt the ghee in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Once melted, add the cabbage and carrots.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the vegetables are reduced in size and slightly browned.
Add the ground beef, water chestnuts, green onions, ginger, salt, and pepper to the pan and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beef is warmed through.
Pour the sauce over the beef mixture and cook for an additional 1 to 2 minutes to let the ͆avors meld, then remove from the heat.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium-sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving it for about 2 minutes, until hot.
Serve the beef mixture in the lettuce leaves, garnished with sesame seeds, with the rice on the side.

name: Sweet Potatoes with Mango Kale Slaw
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: bunch kale, thinly sliced into ¼-inch strips

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the sweet potatoes on the lined baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes, until warmed through.
Meanwhile, make the slaw: Put the olive oil, lime juice, and salt in a medium- sized bowl and whisk together until combined and thickened.
Add the kale to the dressing and massage the dressing into the kale with your hands.
Add the mango, jalapeño, and cilantro to the bowl and toss to coat, then set aside.
To make the jerk pork, place the shredded pork and Jerk Seasoning in a medium- sized bowl and mix to evenly coat the meat in the seasoning.
Pour the olive oil into a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the seasoned pork.
Cook, undisturbed, for 2 to 3 minutes, then ͆ip and cook for an additional 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown.
Remove from the heat.
Cut a slit in each sweet potato, then stuﬀ with the pork and top with the slaw.
Serve!

name: Honey Garlic Pork Skillet
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Place the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds or until fragrant.
Remove the garlic from the pan and set aside.
Spread the pork evenly across the pan and sprinkle with the salt.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the pork starts to brown, then ͆ip and cook for an additional 1 to 2 minutes, until browned on the other side.
Pour the honey sauce and cooked garlic over the browned pork and stir to combine.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce bubbles and begins to reduce.
Reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium-sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving it for about 2 minutes, until hot.
Serve the pork mixture over the rice.
Enjoy!

name: Sweet Potato Tamale Pie
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
To make the ͅlling, place the pork, tomato paste, lime juice, chili powder, cumin, oregano, and salt in a large bowl and stir until fully combined.
Spread the ͅlling in a 3-quart casserole dish or a 10-inch cast-iron skillet, then layer the sweet potato mash over the top.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the pie is warmed through and the sweet potato topping is slightly browned.
Just before the pie is done, thinly slice the avocado and set it aside.
Garnish the pie with the sour cream, sliced avocado, and cilantro and serve!

name: Chorizo and Potato Tacos with Cilantro-Lime Slaw
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: To make the ͅlling, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the potatoes.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, then ͆ip and cook for an additional 3 minutes, until browned and crispy.
Remove the potatoes from the pan and set aside.
Drain all but 1 tablespoon of oil from the pan, then add the pork, salt, spices, and vinegar.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the pork is crispy.
Return the potatoes to the pan and stir them into the pork, then remove the pan from the heat.
To make the slaw, toss the shredded cabbage with the cilantro-lime dressing.
Season to taste with salt.
Place a small skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, put a tortilla in the pan and warm for 30 seconds per side, until the tortilla is pliable and begins to brown slightly.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
To keep them warm while you heat the remaining tortillas, you can wrap them in a kitchen towel.
To assemble the tacos, ͅll each warmed tortilla with the chorizo-potato ͅlling, top with the slaw, and then garnish with the cilantro and cheese.
Serve with lime wedges.

name: Egg Roll in a Bowl
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the onion and garlic and sauté for 2 to 3 minutes, until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the ginger, then add the pork, coconut aminos, vinegar, sesame oil, red pepper ͆akes, and salt.
Stir to combine and cook for 2 minutes, until the sauce begins to bubble.
Add the cabbage, carrots, and green onions to the pan and toss to coat in the sauce.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage and carrots are wilted, then serve!

name: Swedish Meatballs Over Mashed Potatoes
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: salted butter, ghee, or oil of choice
gluten-free ͆our blend, or 1 tablespoon arrowroot powder
heavy cream or full-fat coconut milk

instructions: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Once melted, sprinkle in the ͆our and whisk until smooth.
Pour in the chicken broth ½ cup at a time, whisking constantly to smooth out any lumps.
Bring the mixture to a low boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low and whisk in the cream, salt, and pepper.
Add the meatballs to the pan and stir to coat, then cover and cook for 5 minutes, until heated through.
Before serving, taste the sauce for seasoning and add more salt, if desired.

While the meatballs are warming, reheat the mashed potatoes either by microwaving for 3 minutes, stirring halfway through, or by placing in a small saucepan over medium heat and cooking, covered, for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over the mashed potatoes and garnish with the parsley. note: If using arrowroot powder, bring the broth to a boil in a large skillet.
Meanwhile, stir the arrowroot powder and 2 tablespoons of water together in a small bowl to form a slurry.
Once the broth is boiling, whisk in the slurry.
Boil for 1 minute, until the broth begins to thicken.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and whisk in the cream, salt, and pepper, then proceed to Step 3.

name: Chicken Marsala Casserole
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: salted butter, ghee, or oil of choice
strands scraped from 1 roasted spaghetti squash

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Once hot, add the cooked onion, garlic, and mushroom mixture and sauté for 1 to 2 minutes, until warmed through.
Pour in the wine and broth and boil for 1 minute to cook oﬀ the alcohol, then whisk in the cream, butter, dried parsley, ½ teaspoon of the salt, and ¼ teaspoon of the pepper.
Stir in the prosciutto, then slide the pan oﬀ the heat.
Place the squash strands in an 8-inch round casserole dish and toss with the remaining tablespoon of oil, the garlic powder, remaining ½ teaspoon of salt, and remaining ¼ teaspoon of pepper.
Spread the chicken on top of the squash, then pour the mushroom sauce over the chicken.
Bake for 20 minutes to warm the casserole through.
Garnish with the fresh parsley and serve.

name: Spaghetti Squash Chicken Chow Mein
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: head purple cabbage, cut into 2-inch strips
strands scraped from 1 roasted spaghetti squash

instructions: Heat the oil in a large sauté pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and sauté for and cook for an additional 4 to 5 minutes, until the vegetables are slightly browned.
Stir in the squash strands, chicken, sauce, and green onions.
Toss to combine, then cook for an additional 3 to 4 minutes, until the squash is warmed through and the sauce has started to bubble.
Garnish with the sesame seeds and serve!

name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Soup
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: salted butter, ghee, or oil of choice
fresh lemon juice (about ½ small lemon)

instructions: Melt the butter in a soup pot over medium heat, then add the onion, mushrooms, and garlic.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the onion and mushrooms are slightly browned.
Sprinkle the ͆our blend into the pot and whisk until it has been absorbed into the mushroom mixture.
Pour in the broth 1 cup at a time, whisking constantly to smooth out any lumps.
To the pot, add the cream, mustard, lemon juice, thyme, salt, pepper, and chicken.

Give the soup a stir and cook for about 5 minutes, until the chicken is warmed through, then serve. note: If using arrowroot powder, complete Step 1, then add all of the chicken broth to the pot, cover, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Meanwhile, whisk together the arrowroot powder and ¼ cup water, then stir the slurry into the boiling broth.
Simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until thickened, then reduce the heat to medium and proceed to Step 3.

name: BBQ Brisket Bowls
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Thinly slice the brisket, then put it in a medium-sized bowl along with the spice rub.
Toss to coat the meat in the seasonings.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the seasoned brisket.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then ͆ip each piece and cook for an additional 2 to 3 minutes, until browned on both sides.
Meanwhile, reheat the rice either by placing it in a medium-sized saucepan, covered, over low heat for 5 minutes or by microwaving for about 2 minutes, until hot.
Spoon the warmed rice into bowls and top with the brisket, pickles, onion slices, a drizzle of BBQ sauce, and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro.
Enjoy!

name: Chipotle Brisket Tacos with Green Apple Slaw
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings

ingredients.name: avocado oil mayonnaise or vegan mayo

instructions: Place the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper in a medium-sized bowl and whisk to combine.
Thinly slice the brisket and add it to the bowl with the seasonings.
Toss the meat in the seasoning mixture until well coated.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the seasoned brisket and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then ͆ip and cook for an additional 2 to 3 minutes, until browned on both sides.
Remove from the heat and set aside.
While the brisket is cooking, make the slaw: Cut the apple into ¼-inch-thick matchsticks, to equal 1 cup.
Place the mayonnaise, lemon juice, honey, salt, and pepper in a large bowl and whisk until smooth.
Stir in the apple, Brussels sprouts, and chopped cilantro.
To warm the tortillas, preheat a small skillet over medium-high heat.
Once hot, put a tortilla in the pan and warm for 30 seconds per side, until the tortilla is pliable and begins to brown slightly.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas.
To keep them warm while you heat the remaining tortillas, you can wrap them in a kitchen towel.
Fill each tortilla with brisket and slaw, garnish with a cilantro sprig, and serve!

name: Brisket Fried Rice
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings

ingredients.name: plus 1 teaspoon ghee or avocado oil
plus 2 tablespoons thinly sliced green onions
sprigs fresh cilantro, or 1 tablespoon chopped fresh cilantro

instructions: In a small bowl, whisk the eggs.
Place 1 teaspoon of the ghee in a small skillet over medium-high heat.
Once melted, add the eggs and spread evenly across the pan.
Cook for 2 minutes, then ͆ip and cook for an additional minute, until fully heated through.
Transfer the eggs to a cutting board and cut into ½-inch squares, then set aside.
Cut the brisket into ½-inch cubes.
Heat 1½ tablespoons of the ghee in a large sauté pan or wok over medium-high heat.
Once hot, add the brisket.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned.
Add the ginger and garlic to the pan with the brisket and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the Brussels sprouts and carrots to the pan with the brisket.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the carrots and Brussels sprouts are slightly browned, then stir in ¼ cup of the green onions.
Add the remaining 1½ tablespoons of ghee to the pan and stir it into the meat and vegetable mixture.
Add the rice and toss to combine it with the rest of the ingredients.
Add the eggs, coconut aminos, lime juice, sesame oil, and red pepper ͆akes to the rice mixture and stir to combine.
Add the salt, then taste for seasoning and add more salt, if needed.
Let the rice cook, untouched, for 2 minutes.
Then stir the rice, scraping any browned bits oﬀ of the bottom of the pan.
Cook for an additional 1 to 2 minutes, until the rice is slightly browned and crisp.
Remove from the heat.
Garnish with the remaining 2 tablespoons of green onions and the cilantro and enjoy!

name: Honey Mustard Sheet Pan Dinner
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 5 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Place the shredded pork, half of the honey mustard dressing, and ½ teaspoon of the salt in a medium-sized bowl and toss to coat.
Place the cabbage wedges and potatoes on a rimmed baking sheet.
Drizzle with the olive oil, sprinkle with the pepper and remaining teaspoon of salt, and toss to coat.
Place clumps of the shredded pork mixture on the baking sheet in between the cabbage and potatoes.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the pork is browned and the potatoes and cabbage are warmed through.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, and chop the parsley.
Drizzle the remaining dressing over the potatoes and cabbage, garnish with the parsley, and serve.

name: Enchilada Verde Casserole with Avocado Slaw
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 6 servings

ingredients.name: shredded white cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Make the casserole: In a medium-sized bowl, toss the pork with the chili powder, cumin, oregano, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.

Spread 1 cup of the salsa in an 8-inch square baking dish, then cover with 2 tortillas: place a tortilla in one corner of the dish, then cut the second tortilla in half and use the halves to ͅll in the empty spaces along the side and bottom of the whole tortilla.
Spread one-third of the seasoned pork over the tortillas, then top with 1 cup of the salsa and ¼ cup of the cheese.
Repeat for two more layers.
Bake the casserole, uncovered, for 30 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling.
Meanwhile, make the avocado slaw: In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the lime juice and avocado oil.
Add the onions, jalapeño, avocado, cilantro, and cabbage and toss to coat.
Place the slaw on top of the casserole and serve!
Mini Sloppy Joe–Stuﬀed

name: Lemon Pepper Chicken Breasts
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the lime juice and olive oil.
Place the chicken in the bowl and toss to coat evenly.
Place the chicken on the lined baking sheet, then sprinkle both sides with the paprika, salt, and pepper.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the juices run clear.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

name: Paprika Lime Chicken Breasts
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the lemon juice and olive oil.
Place the chicken in the bowl and toss to coat evenly.
Place the chicken on the lined baking sheet, then sprinkle both sides with the salt and pepper.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the juices run clear.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

name: Crispy Curried Chicken Thighs
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Pour the balsamic vinegar into a medium-sized bowl.
Place the chicken in the bowl and toss to coat evenly.
Place the thighs on the lined baking sheet, then sprinkle with the salt and pepper.
Bake for 25 minutes, or until the juices run clear and the tops are browned.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

name: Balsamic Chicken Thighs
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a medium-sized bowl, whisk together the lime juice and curry powder.
Place the chicken in the bowl and toss to coat evenly.
Place the thighs, skin side up, on the lined baking sheet, then sprinkle both sides with the salt and pepper.
Bake for 45 minutes, or until the juices run clear and the tops are browned.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

name: Ranch Chicken Thighs
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Sprinkle both sides of the pork chops with the rub.
Place a medium-sized ovenproof skillet over medium heat and pour in the olive oil.
Once the oil thins from the heat, after about 30 seconds, add the pork chops.
Sear the chops for about 3 minutes, or until slightly golden on one side.
Flip the chops over and transfer to the oven to bake for 12 minutes, or until the juices run clear.
Let the chops rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

name: Simple Seared Pork Chops
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
Pour the ranch dressing into a medium-sized bowl.
Place the chicken in the bowl and toss to coat evenly.
Place the thighs on the lined baking sheet, then sprinkle both sides with the salt and pepper.
Bake for 25 minutes, or until the juices run clear and the tops are browned.

Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before cutting. pro tip: If you want these pork chops to be extra juicy, let them sit in a refrigerated brine of 2 cups water plus 2 tablespoons sea salt and 2 tablespoons maple syrup for a minimum of 4 hours or a maximum of 24 hours.
Pat dry and proceed with the cooking instructions above.

name: Southwestern Pork Chops
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Heat the olive oil in a large cast-iron or other ovenproof skillet over high heat.
While the oil heats, sprinkle all sides of the tenderloin with the rub.
Once the oil has thinned from the heat, sear the tenderloin on all sides for about and bake for 25 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the pork reads 160°F.

Let the pork rest for 10 minutes before cutting. pro tip: If you want these pork chops to be extra juicy, let them sit in a refrigerated brine of 2 cups water plus 2 tablespoons sea salt and 2 tablespoons maple syrup for a minimum of 4 hours or a maximum of 24 hours.
Pat dry and proceed with the cooking instructions above.

Sear the chops for about 3 minutes, or until slightly golden on one side.
Flip the chops over and transfer to the oven to bake for 12 minutes, or until the juices run clear.
Let the chops rest for 5 minutes before cutting.

description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Heat the olive oil in a large cast-iron or other ovenproof skillet over high heat.
While the oil heats, sprinkle all sides of the tenderloin with the seasoning.
Once the oil has thinned from the heat, sear the tenderloin on all sides for about and bake for 25 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the pork reads 160°F.
Let the pork rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Heat the olive oil in a large cast-iron or other ovenproof skillet over high heat.
While the oil heats, whisk the mustard, honey, salt, and pepper together in a bowl.
Spread the honey mustard evenly over the pork tenderloin.
Once the oil has thinned from the heat, sear the tenderloin on all sides for about and bake for 25 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the pork reads 160°F.
Let the pork rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Easy Tuna Steak
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sprinkle both sides of the ͅsh with the salt and pepper.
Once the oil has thinned from the heat, sear the ͅsh for 2 minutes per side, or until a light brown crust develops.
Sprinkle the cooked ͅsh with the lemon juice.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Pan-Seared White Fish
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sprinkle both sides of the tuna with the salt and pepper.

Once the oil has thinned from the heat, sear the tuna for 2 minutes per side, or until a light brown crust develops on the outside and the inside is still pink. (This cook time results in medium-done tuna; if you like your tuna slightly more or less well-done, adjust the time accordingly.)
Let the tuna rest for 5 to 10 minutes before serving.
Enjoy warm or chilled and sliced over a salad.

name: Lemon-Garlic Shrimp
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Sprinkle the shrimp with the garlic powder and salt.
Add the shrimp to the skillet and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook for 3 minutes per side, or until pink.
Once cooked, add the lemon juice and stir to combine.
Serve immediately.

name: Pan-Seared Salmon
description: From Cook Once, Eat All Week cookbook - 4 servings
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sprinkle the salmon ͅllets with the salt and pepper.
Sear the salmon on each side for 3 minutes, or until the ͅsh ͆akes at the thickest part.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Slow Cooker Mediterranean Beef with Tzatziki
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 6 servings
instructions: Add the oil to a large, heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the beef and sear it for 3 to 4 minutes, until it is brown.
Flip the beef and cook it for 3 to 4 minutes, until it is brown.
Transfer the beef to a large slow cooker.
You can skip this step, but it adds flavor and color.
If you choose to skip this step, omit the oil from the recipe.In a small bowl, mix together the oregano, salt, cumin, coriander, black pepper, and allspice.
Sprinkle this mixture over the beef in the slow cooker and stir to coat the beef.
Stir in the onion and garlic.
Cook the beef on low for 8 hours.To make the tzatziki, finely grate the cucumber.
Use a paper towel or kitchen towel to squeeze out as much of the cucumber’s moisture as possible.
Transfer the cucumber to a medium bowl.
Add the yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, lemon zest, oil, dill, black pepper, and salt to taste.
Stir to combine the ingredients.
Place the tzatziki in the fridge to chill for at least 2 hours before serving.Serve the beef drizzled with the tzatziki in a pita, over rice, or on a bed of greens.

name: Cashew Chicken and Pineapple Fried Rice
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 4 servings

ingredients.name: coarsely chopped cooked boneless, skinless chicken

instructions: Add the eggs.
Scramble the eggs for 1 to 2 minutes, until they are just cooked through.
Remove the eggs from the skillet and set them aside.Add the remaining 1 tablespoon (15 g) of oil to the skillet.
Add the green onions, garlic, Asian garlic chili paste (if using), and ginger.
Cook the mixture for 30 seconds.
Add the pineapple, bell pepper, and peas and carrots.
Cook the mixture for 3 to 4 minutes, until the pineapple begins to caramelize.
Add the rice, chicken, and cashews.
Stir to combine the ingredients.Press the rice into the bottom of the skillet with the back of a spoon.
Cook the rice for 2 to 3 minutes, until it begins to turn brown and crispy.
Repeat this step if desired for more crispy rice.Stir in the scrambled eggs and soy sauce.
Taste and add more soy sauce as needed.Kitchen Hack: Don’t have time to prep the rice or chicken?
Let the grocery store do the heavy lifting.
Grab some frozen brown rice and cook it for two-thirds of the suggested cooking time.
Then grab a rotisserie chicken or some cooked chicken breast.
You can even grab the green onions, red bell pepper, and pineapple from the salad bar.

name: Baked Pizza Pork Chops with Cauliflower
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 2 servings
instructions: Add some sauce and cheese, and I can get them to eat just about anything.

We usually do this with veggies, although lately I have been trying it with proteins—it works like a charm.Serves: 2Total Time: 35 minutes2 cups (460 g) cauliflower florets1 tbsp (15 ml) olive oil, divided1 tsp Italian seasoning, dividedSalt, as neededBlack pepper, as needed2 (5-oz [140-g]) lean boneless pork chops½ tsp garlic powder⅔ cup (160 ml) spaghetti sauce⅓ cup (37 g) shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese2 tbsp (20 g) coarsely chopped turkey pepperoniPreheat the oven to 400°F (204°C).In a large glass baking dish, toss the cauliflower with ½ tablespoon (8 ml) of the oil, ½ teaspoon of the Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper.

Spread the cauliflower out in a single layer and roast it for 10 minutes, until it is beginning to brown and soften.Meanwhile, brush the pork chops on both sides with the remaining ½ tablespoon (7 ml) of oil.
Sprinkle them with the remaining ½ teaspoon of Italian seasoning, garlic powder, and salt.Carefully remove the baking dish from the oven.
Nestle the pork chops into the dish among the cauliflower.
Cook the pork chops and cauliflower for 12 minutes.Carefully remove the baking dish from the oven and cover the pork chops and cauliflower with the spaghetti sauce.
Sprinkle the mozzarella cheese and pepperoni over top.

Return the baking dish to the oven and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the pork’s internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C).Know Your Ingredients: There are so many different options for jarred pasta sauce, it can be hard to know what to choose.
Always look for a sauce with little or, better yet, no added sugar.
Make sure the ingredient list includes only things you recognize, and avoid sauces with high-fructose corn syrup and added preservatives.

name: Crispy Herb Polenta Fries
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 2 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F (204°C).
Spray a large baking sheet with cooking spray.Cut the polenta into slices that are about ¾ inch (2 cm) thick.
Then cut those slices into fries that are about ¾ inch (2 cm) wide.

Transfer the fries to the prepared baking sheet.Gently toss the polenta fries with the oil, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper.Spread out the polenta fries in a single layer, so that they aren’t touching.
Bake the polenta fries for 30 minutes, flipping them halfway through the cooking time, until they are brown and crispy.
Serve the polenta fries with the spaghetti sauce for dipping.Kitchen Tip: Tubed polenta is one of my favorite pantry staples to grab when I need a quick side dish.
Although fries are our family favorite, you can cut the polenta into cubes for croutons, rounds for an easy appetizer, or “soldiers” for dipping into soup.

name: Skillet Turkey Enchiladas
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 4 servings

ingredients.name: reduced-fat sour cream or cream cheese

instructions: Add the onion and bell pepper.
Cook the vegetables for 4 to 5 minutes, until they are tender.
Add the garlic and cook it for 30 seconds, until it is fragrant.
Add the turkey, cumin, oregano, and salt.
Cook the mixture for 7 to 10 minutes, breaking up the turkey as it cooks, until the turkey is brown and cooked through.
Taste the mixture and season it with additional salt if needed.Stir in the pinto beans, tortillas, and salsa verde.
Cook the mixture for 4 to 5 minutes, until it is heated through and the tortillas are soft.
Stir in the sour cream, if using, until it is fully incorporated.
Add the Cheddar cheese and cover.

Cook the mixture for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese is melted.Top the enchiladas with cilantro, avocado, jalapeños, diced tomatoes, or any other toppings you enjoy.Reheating Tip: If you are using the leftovers for lunch, add some extra salsa before reheating to keep everything moist and delicious.Know Your Ingredients: In this recipe, I opt for salsa verde instead of standard enchilada sauce.
Although enchilada sauce would work, I find the ingredients in salsa to be much cleaner—more veggies, fewer fillers and artificial flavors.
And in case you’re wondering, salsa definitely counts as a serving of veggies.

name: Cheddar-Apple Chicken Burgers
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 2 servings
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, apple, Cheddar cheese, poultry seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Gently combine the ingredients using your hands, and try not to compress the meat.Divide the meat into portions and shape them into patties.
Make a small indent in the center of each patty with your thumb to help it cook more evenly.Heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the burgers and cook them for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, until the burgers’ internal temperature reaches at least 165°F (74°C).

name: Slow Cooker Honey-Soy Chicken
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 6 servings
instructions: Add the chicken thighs to the slow cooker.In a medium bowl, mix together the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, red onion, garlic, ginger, and Asian garlic chili paste (if using).
Pour the sauce over the chicken.
Cook the chicken on low for 4 hours.Remove the chicken and set it aside.
Whisk the cornstarch into the liquid in the slow cooker.
Cover the slow cooker with its lid and increase the heat to high.
Cook the sauce for 15 to 30 minutes, until it thickens to your liking.Meanwhile, slice or shred the chicken.
Transfer it back to the sauce.
Top the chicken with the green onions.Kitchen Hack: If you forget to throw this in your slow cooker, you can always speed things up with a rotisserie chicken.
Simply add the ingredients for the sauce to a small pot over medium heat and simmer it until it thickens.
Then toss the sauce with the sliced rotisserie chicken and serve.

name: Coconut Quinoa
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 4 servings
instructions: Add the quinoa and coconut.
Toast them for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until they are light brown.
Add the coconut milk, water, brown sugar, and salt.Bring the quinoa to a boil and stir.
Reduce the heat to low.
Cover the quinoa and cook it for 15 minutes.Without uncovering the pot, turn off the heat and let the quinoa sit for 5 minutes, or until it is fluffy and the liquid is absorbed.
Fluff the quinoa with a fork.Make It Your Own: We love adding some fresh lime juice to this dish, along with either chopped fresh cilantro or green onions.
If you prefer something sweeter, use sweetened shredded coconut in place of the unsweetened.
Trying to sneak in veggies?
Throw in some cauliflower rice.
It blends right in with the quinoa.

name: Spicy Asian Brussels Sprouts
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 2 servings
instructions: Preheat the oven to 450°F (232°C).
Spray a large baking sheet with cooking spray.In a large bowl, toss the Brussels sprouts with the oil.
Lightly season them with the salt and black pepper.
Place the Brussels sprouts in a single layer on the baking sheet, leaving some space between the Brussels sprouts.
They shouldn’t overlap.

Roast the Brussels sprouts for 20 to 25 minutes, or until they are brown and crispy.Meanwhile, in a small saucepan over medium heat, combine the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, Asian garlic chili paste, and garlic powder.
Bring the mixture to a simmer and cook it for 3 to 4 minutes, until it thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove the sauce from the heat.Toss the hot Brussels sprouts with the sauce and serve.

name: Creamy Spinach and Artichoke Pasta
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 2 servings
instructions: Add the shallot, garlic, and artichoke hearts to the pot.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often.Add the broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Add the pasta.
Bring the mixture back to a boil, and then reduce the heat to medium-low.

Cover the pot and cook the pasta for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring halfway through the cooking time, until the pasta is al dente and has absorbed most of the liquid.Stir in the spinach and cook until it wilts.
Stir in the Parmesan cheese, cream cheese, and cooked chicken.
Remove the pot from the heat and let the mixture rest for 5 minutes to allow the sauce to thicken.
Season the pasta with the salt and black pepper.

name: Broiled Barbecue Flank Steak with Mango Salsa
description: From Stress-Free Family Meal Planning - 4 servings
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, chili powder, and black pepper.
Set the spice rub aside.Place the steak on the foil-lined baking sheet.
Broil the steak for 4 to 5 minutes.
Carefully flip the steak over and cover the top with the spice rub.
Broil the steak for 4 to 5 minutes, until it is brown and its internal temperature reaches 140°F (60°C) for medium doneness.
Adjust the cooking time depending on your desired level of doneness.
Remove the steak from the oven and tent it with foil.
Let the steak rest for 10 minutes.Meanwhile, make the mango salsa.

In a medium bowl, mix together the mango, jalapeño (if using), onion, cilantro, lime juice, salt, and black pepper.Slice the steak very thinly against the grain and serve it with the mango salsa.Kitchen Tip: During spring and summer, we make this dish on the grill.
